mainTopic: The end of the dispute about leftover חטאת blood, and the משנה of the עולה: its holiness, how its blood is placed (רב and שמואל, and the תנאים), and why the southeast corner of the מזבח had no יסוד.
overview: This amud opens by closing an earlier dispute with one last version: the school of רבי ישמעאל reports that רבי שמעון בן יוחי agrees with them that leftover blood of all חטאות goes to the western יסוד. A memory sign follows. Then a new משנה lists the laws of the עולה. The גמרא explains that the משנה calls the עולה קדשי קדשים because no פסוק says so outright. Next it asks how the 'two placements that are four' are done. רב says each corner gets two separate placements, and שמואל says each corner gets one gamma-shaped placement. A ברייתא shows the same argument between תנאים, and רבי ישמעאל learns four separate placements from the חטאת. The ברייתא explains that the עולה uses only two corners because it needs a יסוד, and the southeast corner had none. The גמרא traces this to the tribal border: that corner stood on a strip of יהודה's land, which בנימין longed for every day. The פסוק that proves this comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Another version: both kinds of leftover blood go to the western base
steps.stepSummary: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches that רבי שמעון בן יוחי agrees with them: leftover blood from both inner and outer חטאות is poured at the western base. A memory sign is given to help remember this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught, in line with רבי שמעון בן יוחי: both this and that go to the western base. Your memory sign: 'The men pulled the man.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the earlier discussion about leftover חטאת blood with one more version of who holds what. It adds a short memory sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רבי שמעון בן יוחי holds that both the inner and the outer חטאת have their leftover blood poured at the western יסוד. That means he agrees with רבי ישמעאל. The memory sign pictures the many students of רבי ישמעאל ('the men') pulling רבי שמעון בן יוחי ('the man') over to their teacher's side.

keyTerms.meaning: The study house (school) of רבי ישמעאל
This and that (both kinds of חטאת)
The western base of the מזבח
Your memory sign

steps.whatToRemember: In this final version, רבי שמעון בן יוחי agrees that all leftover חטאת blood goes to the western יסוד. Remember it with 'the men pulled the man.'
steps.confusionAlert: 'This and that' does not mean two people. It means the two kinds of חטאת, the inner one and the outer one.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught
in line with Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai, they say:
Both this and that go to the western base.
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means the leftover blood of the inner חטאת and of the outer חטאת.

phrases.english: And your memory sign: the men pulled the man.
phrases.notes: The 'men' are רבי ישמעאל's many students, and they 'pull' רבי שמעון בן יוחי over to their teacher's view.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the earlier discussion (before this section) about where leftover חטאת blood is poured.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to this version, רבי שמעון בן יוחי agrees with רבי ישמעאל that leftover blood of both inner and outer חטאות goes to the western יסוד.

steps.title: The laws of the burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists the rules of the עולה. It is קדשי קדשים, it is slaughtered in the north, and its blood is received in the north. Its blood gets two placements that are four. It is skinned and cut up, and it is burned completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: The עולה is קדשי קדשים. It is slaughtered in the north, and its blood is received in a holy vessel in the north. Its blood needs two placements that make four. It must be skinned and cut into pieces, and it is entirely burned on the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lays out the basic laws of the עולה, the burnt offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the חטאת, the עולה is slaughtered and has its blood received in the north. Its blood is placed differently, though: two placements on two opposite corners that end up touching all four sides. Unlike other offerings, nothing of it is eaten. It is skinned, cut up, and burned completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Burnt offering, completely burned on the מזבח
Most-holy offerings, the highest level of holiness
A holy vessel used in the מקדש service
Two placements that count as four
Skinning and cutting into pieces
Entirely burned on the fire

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the גמרא here unpacks the lines of this משנה one at a time.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The burnt offering is of the most-holy offerings;
its slaughter is in the north,
and the receiving of its blood in a holy vessel is in the north,

phrases.aramaic: וְדָמָהּ טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע,
phrases.english: and its blood needs two placements that are four,
phrases.notes: Two placements on two opposite corners. Each one touches two sides, so all four sides of the מזבח get blood.

phrases.english: and it needs skinning and cutting into pieces,
and it is entirely for the fires.
phrases.notes: Everything is burned on the מזבח except the hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about a new offering, the עולה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עולה is קדשי קדשים, slaughtered and received in the north, gets two placements that are four, is skinned and cut up, and is completely burned.

steps.title: Why call the burnt offering most holy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to say that the עולה is קדשי קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה teach that the עולה is קדשי קדשים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. It asks why the תנא bothered to call the עולה 'most holy.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה about the חטאת did not stop to say that the חטאת is קדשי קדשים. So why spell it out here for the עולה? The גמרא wants to know what this extra phrase adds.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
He (the תנא) taught it

phrases.english: Gemara:
A burnt offering, what is the reason
that he teaches it as most holy?
phrases.notes: The earlier משנה about the חטאת didn't say 'most holy,' so the extra words here stand out.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹלָה מַאי טַעְמָא תָּנֵי לֵיהּ קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the first phrase of the משנה in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה explicitly labels the עולה as קדשי קדשים.

steps.title: Because the Torah never says it outright
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the Torah never writes 'it is most holy' about the עולה, so the משנה had to tell us.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because about the עולה it is not written, 'it is most holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The Torah writes 'most holy' about the חטאת and the אשם, but never about the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was no need to say it about the חטאת, because a פסוק already calls it most holy. For the עולה there is no such פסוק. So the משנה tells us directly that the עולה is also קדשי קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not written

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה mentions that the עולה is קדשי קדשים only because the Torah never says so in plain words, as it does for the חטאת and אשם.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the עולה is less holy. It is fully קדשי קדשים. The משנה simply had to say it, since no פסוק does.

phrases.english: Because it is not written about it
"(to the Lord) it is most holy."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:10, said about the חטאת and אשם. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The Torah writes 'most holy' explicitly for the חטאת and אשם but not for the עולה, so the משנה states it.

steps.title: How are the two placements done?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about two placements and asks how the כהן actually does them.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And its blood needs two placements.' How does he do it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It asks for the practical method of placing the blood. This sets up the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says 'two placements that are four,' but it does not explain how two can count as four. The גמרא wants the actual procedure at the corners of the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: How does he do it?
A placement (of blood)

phrases.english: 'And its blood needs two placements.'
How does he do it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדָמָהּ טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת. הֵיכִי עָבֵיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a different line of the משנה in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical way the כהן places the blood so that two placements count as four.

steps.title: רב: place, then place again
steps.stepSummary: רב says the כהן puts blood on one side of the corner and then again on the other side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: He places, and then goes back and places again.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer. At each corner the כהן makes two separate placements, one on each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, the 'four' is made of separate placements: two at one corner and two at the opposite corner, one for each side. The 'two' in the משנה refers to the two corners.

keyTerms.meaning: He places, and places again

phrases.english: Rav said:
He places, and goes back and places again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two separate placements at each of two corners, one on each side.

steps.title: שמואל: one placement shaped like a gamma
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the כהן makes one placement at each corner, bent around it like the Greek letter gamma, so it covers both sides at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: He makes one placement, shaped like a gamma.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different method. One placement wraps around the corner and touches both sides together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שמואל, each of the two placements is a single action that bends around the corner like an 'L.' One placement covers two sides, so two placements at opposite corners cover all four sides.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the shape of a gamma (Greek letter shaped like Γ, a right angle)

steps.whatToRemember: רב: two separate placements at each corner. שמואל: one bent, gamma-shaped placement at each corner. Either way, all four sides of the מזבח get blood.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
He places one placement, like a gamma.
phrases.notes: A gamma looks like Γ, a right angle, so the blood wraps around the corner onto both sides.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מַתָּנָה אַחַת כְּמִין גַּמָּא נוֹתֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רב's to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One gamma-shaped placement at each of two corners, covering both sides of each corner.

steps.title: A ברייתא that matches שמואל's gamma-shape view
steps.stepSummary: The argument between רב and שמואל is like an older argument between תנאים. The first opinion in the ברייתא works out the gamma shape from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like an argument between תנאים. You might think the כהן throws the blood just once. So the פסוק says 'around.' But if it says 'around,' maybe he should run the blood all the way around the מזבח like a thread? So the פסוק says 'and sprinkle.' How does this work? In a gamma shape. Its blood needs two placements that are really four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the argument between רב and שמואל already shows up in a ברייתא. The first opinion in that ברייתא sounds just like שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'around' rules out one single throw. The word 'sprinkle' rules out running the blood all the way around like a thread. The middle path is one placement bent around a corner, which reaches two sides at once. Two of those placements cover four sides, which is exactly שמואל's gamma.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like an argument between תנאים, the rabbis of the משנה period
The פסוק teaches us
Around
Like a thread, meaning one unbroken line all the way around
Two placements that count as four, because each one reaches two sides

steps.confusionAlert: In this first opinion (like שמואל), 'two placements that are four' means two actions, each covering two sides of the מזבח. רב (step 6) and רבי ישמעאל (next step) instead read it as four separate placements.

phrases.english: This is like a dispute between tannaim:
One might think he should sprinkle it with one sprinkling?
The verse states: "around."
If "around," one might think he should encircle it like a thread?
The verse states: "and sprinkle."
How so? In the shape of a gamma –

phrases.aramaic: וְדָמָהּ טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע.
phrases.english: and its blood requires two placements that are four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties שמואל's view from step 7 to an older ברייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first opinion in the ברייתא, which reads 'around' and 'sprinkle' together

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל compares the עולה to the חטאת
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל learns from the shared word 'around' that the עולה needs four separate placements, like the חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: The Torah says 'around' here, and it says 'around' there too. Just as there the blood was put in separate placements, four of them, so too here it goes in separate placements, four of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives the second opinion in the ברייתא. He compares the עולה to the חטאת because the same word appears in both places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת that משה brought got four separate placements of blood. Since the same word 'around' appears with the עולה, the עולה also gets four separate placements, not two bent ones. This matches רב.

keyTerms.meaning: It says here, and it says there: a way of comparing two topics through a shared word
Separate, broken-up placements, not one continuous line
Placements of blood on the מזבח

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
It is stated here: "around,"
and it is stated there: "around";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 8:15, about the חטאת משה brought at the start of the משכן.

phrases.english: just as there it is separate placements, four of them,
so too here it is separate placements, four of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: נֶאֱמַר כָּאן ״סָבִיב״, וְנֶאֱמַר לְהַלָּן ״סָבִיב״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The other side of the argument between the תנאים, matching רב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The עולה gets four separate placements, learned from the חטאת

steps.title: Why not all four corners, like the חטאת?
steps.stepSummary: If the עולה is compared to the חטאת, it should also get blood on all four corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so: just as there the four placements went on the four corners, so too here, four placements should go on the four corners!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges רבי ישמעאל's comparison. It asks why the comparison does not go all the way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חטאת got one placement on each of the four corners. If the עולה is learned from the חטאת, it should also use all four corners. But רבי ישמעאל's system uses only two corners, two placements on each.

keyTerms.meaning: The corners (literally 'horns') of the מזבח
If so, used here to push a comparison further

phrases.english: If so – just as there
it is four placements on four corners,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן אַרְבַּע מַתָּנוֹת עַל אַרְבַּע קְרָנוֹת?!
phrases.english: so too here, four placements on four corners?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי – מָה לְהַלָּן אַרְבַּע מַתָּנוֹת עַל אַרְבַּע קְרָנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes רבי ישמעאל's comparison to its full extent
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's comparison between the עולה and the חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison would require all four corners, not just two

steps.title: The עולה needs a corner with a יסוד
steps.stepSummary: The עולה's blood must go where there is a יסוד below, and the southeast corner had none, so it cannot use all four corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: You yourself said that an עולה needs a יסוד. And the southeast corner had no יסוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the challenge. The comparison to the חטאת stops at the corners because of a separate rule about the עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עולה's blood must be placed above the יסוד, the base of the מזבח. The southeast corner had no יסוד under it, so not every corner qualifies. That is why the עולה uses two corners that do have a יסוד, northeast and southwest, which sit across from each other.

keyTerms.meaning: You (already) said, pointing to a rule that is already known
The base step at the bottom of the מזבח
The southeast corner

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the עולה's blood goes on two opposite corners and not all four.

phrases.english: You said: a burnt offering requires a base;
and the southeast corner
did not have a base.

steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate rule limits how far the comparison goes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עולה should copy the חטאת completely, using all four corners
steps.terutzMaskana: The עולה needs a יסוד, and one corner has none, so it uses only the two opposite corners that do

steps.title: Why did the southeast corner have no יסוד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the southeast corner lacked a יסוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the southeast corner of the מזבח was built without a יסוד. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 relied on the fact that the southeast corner had no base. Now the גמרא wants to know why the מזבח was built that way.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the fact used in step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the southeast corner had no יסוד

steps.title: That corner was not in בנימין's land
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the southeast corner was not in the land of the tribe of בנימין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Because it was not in the portion of the one who tears.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers that the southeast corner stood outside בנימין's portion of land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The one who tears' refers to בנימין, whom יעקב called a wolf that tears. The southeast corner was not on בנימין's land, so no יסוד was built there.

keyTerms.meaning: His portion of land
The one who tears, meaning the tribe of בנימין

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל טוֹרֵף.
phrases.english: Because it was not in the portion of the one who tears.
phrases.notes: This means בנימין, called 'a wolf that tears' in בראשית 49:27.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: לְפִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל טוֹרֵף
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The southeast corner was not in בנימין's land, so it had no יסוד

steps.title: The מזבח reached one אמה into יהודה's land
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק teaches that the מזבח took up one אמה of יהודה's land, which supports רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: The מזבח 'eats' one אמה of יהודה's portion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי אלעזר. Part of the מזבח stood on יהודה's land, not בנימין's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזבח stood mostly on בנימין's land, but one אמה of it reached into יהודה's land. That strip was at the southeast corner of the base, so no יסוד was built there.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'eats'; here it means 'takes up' space
A cubit, a measure of length

steps.whatToRemember: The עולה's blood goes on two opposite corners that have a יסוד, northeast and southwest. The southeast corner had no יסוד because that part of the מזבח stood on יהודה's land.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: As Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:

phrases.aramaic: מִזְבֵּחַ אוֹכֵל בְּחֶלְקוֹ שֶׁל יְהוּדָה אַמָּה.
phrases.english: The altar takes up one cubit of the portion of Judah.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אלעזר's answer in step 13
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's claim that the southeast corner was not in בנימין's land
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק's teaching that the מזבח took up one אמה of יהודה's land

steps.title: A strip of יהודה's land entered בנימין's portion, and בנימין longed for it
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי בר חמא, quoting רבי חמא ברבי חנינא, teaches that a narrow strip of יהודה's land stuck out into בנימין's portion. The righteous בנימין was pained every day, wanting to take it. A פסוק is about to be brought as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי בר חמא said in the name of רבי חמא ברבי חנינא: a narrow strip of land came out of יהודה's portion and went into בנימין's portion. בנימין the righteous was pained over it every day, wanting to take it for himself, as the פסוק says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another teaching that explains how part of the מזבח could stand on יהודה's land while the rest was in בנימין's land. It ends by setting up a פסוק that comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13-14 said that one corner of the מזבח stood on יהודה's land. This teaching shows how that could happen: a thin strip of יהודה's land pushed into בנימין's area. It also adds something new: בנימין felt the loss and wished every day that this holy spot were his.

keyTerms.meaning: A strip; here, a narrow strip of land
His portion; a tribe's share of ארץ ישראל
בנימין the righteous; the tribe of בנימין, praised here
Pained, troubled, longing
To take it for himself
As it is said; introduces a פסוק as the source

steps.confusionAlert: The statement does not finish here. The word שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר opens a פסוק, and the פסוק comes at the start of the next amud.
steps.whyThisMatters: This picture of the land is the background for the missing יסוד at the southeast corner. It explains why the עולה's blood could not be put on all four corners.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi bar Ḥama said
that Rabbi Ḥama, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
A strip of land came out
phrases.notes: This is the strip of יהודה's land that the last steps were talking about, where part of the מזבח stood.

phrases.english: from the portion of Judah
and went into the portion of Benjamin,
and Benjamin the righteous
was pained over it every day,
wanting to take it,
as it is said:
